grounding.excerpt: There shall be no discharge of visible films of oil, globules of oil, grease or solids in or on the water, or coatings on stream banks.

FLOATING SOLIDS, VISIBLE FOAM AND/OR OILS

There shall be no discharge of floating solids or visible foam in other than trace amounts.
There shall be no discharge of visible films of oil, globules of oil, grease or solids in or on
the water, or coatings on stream banks.

payload.rationale: The nominated prohibition is stated in Part I under the heading FLOATING SOLIDS, VISIBLE FOAM AND/OR OILS using mandatory effluent-limitation language ("There shall be no discharge"), alongside an adjacent qualitative prohibition on floating solids and visible foam in the same section. The criteria—visible films, globules, grease or solids in or on the water, and coatings on stream banks—are expressed without any numeric concentration, daily maximum, or monthly average, and inherently require visual or qualitative observation rather than laboratory numeric comparison. Part I.C.6–7 frames excursion reporting and violation evidence around daily maximum or monthly average values on the Discharge Monitoring Report, establishing a numeric exceedance comparison pathway that does not map onto this qualitative prohibition. On the available packet evidence, the nominated clause should be classified as an enforceable effluent limitation that falls outside numeric exceedance comparison and instead requires qualitative or visual compliance evaluation. The sampling-location sentence is present but its referent ("monitoring requirements specified above") is ambiguous relative to this clause; that ambiguity does not defeat the classification supported by the limitation text and the numeric excursion framework.
